title: Pilot hedging and safe rollback checkpoint
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-03 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Helix ML), Tom Alvarez (Helix Eng), Sara Nguyen (Helix Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on model selection hedging, version pin strategy, and a concrete rollback/checkpoint plan. Reviewed recent latency and token-cost tradeoffs, validated fallback rules for hosted vs dedicated, and agreed on a short benchmark plan and security doc follow-up.
topics: Failover paths: hosted -> dedicated -> lightweight quantized variant
Security and VPC considerations for rollback testing
Benchmarks to run before freeze window
action_items: Maya Chen - Send updated pricing + burst capacity options and a mapping table for model variants - 2026-12-06
Liam O'Connor - Share micro-benchmark script and baseline commands for latency/cost (seq len 128 / batch 8) - 2026-12-04
Priya Kapoor - Run seeded evals on top-3 candidate models and upload CSV to shared drive - 2026-12-10
Tom Alvarez - Schedule a 1-hour dry-run in staging for rollback playbook with SSO disabled - 2026-12-09
Sara Nguyen - Confirm required logs/audit retention for compliance and notify Redwood on specific syslog endpoints - 2026-12-07
next_steps: Redwood to provide a hedging matrix that maps latency tiers to model variants and cost impact
Customer to run seeded evals and return quality deltas by 12/10
Schedule rollback dry-run in staging and invite SRE/CSM
Exchange security checklist and KMS/HSM integration notes
transcript:
15:00:02 Maya: alright welcome everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do the usual 45 minute-ish sync today, main goals: pin strategy and safe rollback checkpoint, plus any surprises from your evals
15:00:18 Priya: thanks Maya, yeah we had a couple of runs overnight, some weird latency spikes on the mid-tier model, so we want to talk about hedging and how fast we can swap back to a smaller model without user impact
15:00:35 Liam: quick note — the mid-tier you mentioned, is that the redwood-curated 'archon-s' variant or the community quantized?
15:00:41 Priya: I think it's the archon-s that came from the catalog, but the quantized 4-bit variant is what we used in staging for cost savings, might be a mismatch there, sorry if i'm mixing names
15:00:53 Maya: no worries, names get messy on these calls, totally normal. Tom, are those spikes reproducible when you run your load script?
15:01:05 Tom: somewhat, we saw them mostly at peak concurrency around 400 rps, the 95th tail went up by 120 ms which pushed some of our UI timeouts, so that was a red flag
15:01:17 Sara: from security side we also want to understand the rollback routes because fallback to hosted vs dedicated has different audit implications, we need to know which logs flow where
15:01:30 Liam: yep agreed. For hedging we typically advise a primary/secondary/tertiary matrix: primary is your preferred model pinned for quality, secondary is a faster quantized variant in the same family, tertiary is a smaller architecture we keep warm for hot swaps. That reduces risk of a big quality cliff
15:01:50 Priya: does that require keeping KV cache warm across models? Our sessions have sticky prompts and we worry about cold K-V cache misses causing warmup latency
15:02:03 Liam: good call — you can preserve prefix KV by using the same tokenizer and compatible KV layout, but if architecture differs (like moving from archon-s to archon-micro) you do lose cache compatibility. In that case we recommend a brief warmed shadow path so first requests hit the smaller model once primed
15:02:25 Maya: and on the flip side, we can do a soft-fallback where we route a small percentage of traffic to the secondary for 10-15 minutes before switching over full, gives you a safety net on quality and perf
15:02:38 Tom: how does that look operationally? Do we need dedicated GPUs for the tertiary or can we use burst capacity?
15:02:45 Liam: you can use burst capacity for tertiary in Redwood Dedicated or hosted burst pools, but be careful with cold-start times if the instance isn't kept warm. We have a burst-pricing add-on that Maya will share
15:02:56 Maya: noted, i'll include the burst table. Also the pricing differ if you pin a dedicated pool vs pay-per-use on hosted. We'll show you the delta in the matrix
15:03:12 Priya: on quality, our seeded evals show archon-s gives the best F1 on our taxonomy, archon-quant loses about 2.6 points but reduces per-token by ~40%, and the smaller archon-lite loses 7-9 points but halves latency on avg
15:03:29 Maya: that's the exact kind of tradeoff we want to capture in the hedging matrix — do you have those CSVs uploaded?
15:03:36 Priya: not yet, we plan to upload by Friday, working on normalizing labels across tests
15:03:44 Liam: for the rollback checkpoint plan, our recommended steps: 1) create a freeze window 2) run the staging dry-run of the swap 3) validate telemetry and golden prompts 4) trigger full cutover if thresholds pass, else automatic revert after X minutes. We can codify this in an ops runbook
15:04:03 Tom: what thresholds do you recommend for auto revert? should it be SLO breach or quality delta?
15:04:10 Liam: we usually combine both. e.g., revert if 95th latency increases > 150ms or if quality drop on golden set > 5% after 30 minutes. Those numbers are configurable per workload
15:04:23 Sara: and from compliance side, during a revert we need preserved audit trails for every request and decision point, timestamps, who initiated the rollback. Does Redwood log the decision markers?
15:04:35 Maya: yes, we write rollback events into the console timeline and you can export audit logs. For Private deployments we can forward syslog to your SIEM. We'll note specifics in the security checklist
15:04:50 Priya: can you clarify the difference between 'soft-fallback' and 'hard switch' in your playbook?
15:04:56 Liam: soft-fallback = progressive traffic shifting, keep both models serving and route N% to secondary to test. Hard switch = change primary pointer to secondary and drain the old variant. Soft helps catching quality regressions without full user impact
15:05:10 Tom: if we do soft-fallback how do we compare outputs to detect quality drift? Can we do shadow scoring?
15:05:18 Liam: yes shadow scoring is supported — you can mirror responses to a scoring pipeline. Redwood Optimize has a lightweight runner for that, we'll include an example. Note that shadowing adds cost; we usually sample 2-5% of traffic for scoring
15:05:33 Priya: speaking of cost, can you show how latency and per-token delta look on the matrix? Numbers from our runs: archon-s p95 230ms cost $0.014/token, archon-quant p95 180ms cost $0.009/token, archon-lite p95 110ms cost $0.005/token
15:05:50 Maya: good — we'll translate that into expected monthly delta under your traffic profile and include a tipping point for when switching saves >10% spend without dropping below your quality bar
15:06:01 Tom: one more infra Q — for VPC private deployments, if we do a failover to hosted during an outage, is there anything we need to pre-authorize network-wise?
15:06:12 Liam: yes, hosted fallback requires opening ingress from Redwood egress IP ranges; for Private we can set up a controlled peering/failover path but that needs pre-approved CIDR and firewall rules. We'll document minimal network changes for the planned dry-run
15:06:28 Sara: also want KMS handling clarified: if we roll to hosted variant, are keys still in our HSM? how are encrypted logs handled?
15:06:38 Maya: short answer: hosted requires you to bring-your-own-key via a supported KMS integration if you want to keep key control; logs are encrypted in transit and at rest, but HSM-backed key rotation for hosted is a feature we support for enterprise customers, details in security doc we'll share
15:06:56 Priya: let's talk about the benchmark plan. Liam you mentioned a micro-benchmark script?
15:07:01 Liam: yes it's a simple runner that measures cold vs warm latencies, KV cache hits, and tokenized token cost, built on top of the Redwood CLI. I'll share commands, but high level: seq len 128, batch 8, concurrent 100, and a tail test with 400 concurrency for p95/p99
15:07:20 Tom: any special flags to simulate prefix caching?
15:07:25 Liam: include --prefix-fill to simulate warmed cache and --clear-cache for cold starts; we also have a --shadow-score option to mirror outputs into the local scorer
15:07:36 Priya: in our last run we saw a garbage-collection-like pause on the quant variant, maybe memory pressure on the worker, could be due to tokenization mismatch or large kv objects
15:07:48 Liam: that's likely memory fragmentation on the 4-bit runtimes, we can tweak kernel flags and the batch size. For safety you can set a max-concurrent-per-worker ceiling to avoid head-of-line blocking
15:08:01 Maya: quick pause — any blockers preventing the dry-run next week?
15:08:06 Tom: only SSO and some firewall approvals, Sara is working that list, otherwise good
15:08:12 Sara: yes i'll compile the firewall and logging endpoints and send to Maya by Monday
15:08:18 Priya: one small ask: can we have a pre-defined golden prompt set exported from Redwood so we don't accidentally bias our seeded evals?
15:08:26 Liam: we can export a stable golden set from our evals system. We'll match it to your taxonomy so comparisons align. Also recommend using a 200-sample set for initial gating
15:08:40 Maya: ok, so next: Liam will share the micro-benchmark commands and a sample runbook, Priya will upload evals, Sara will confirm security endpoints, Tom will schedule the staging dry-run. We'll regroup after you have evals and pricing matrix
15:08:58 Speaker 2: (inaudible)
15:09:05 Priya: one more question on automated rollback: if an automatic revert triggers, is there a manual override to keep the secondary?
15:09:12 Liam: yes manual override exists in the console — you can force keep secondary and mark the auto-rollback suppressed, but that action is recorded in audit logs and can require additional approvals if your account has RBAC strict mode enabled
15:09:26 Sara: how granular is RBAC? Can we restrict rollbacks to a small set of SREs?
15:09:32 Maya: yes roles can be scoped to teams and actions; we'll include a recommended RBAC policy for pilot participants in the security checklist
15:09:48 Tom: any recommendations for the revert delay window? 30 mins feels long, but 10 might be too short to capture downstream effects
15:09:56 Liam: 15-30 minutes is common; for UI-facing features we lean 15 minutes, for batch workflows we allow 30. We can tune per-route
15:10:08 Priya: let's carve out an emergency 'deadman's switch' procedure in the runbook — e.g., codepath to immediately flip to tertiary and throttle traffic if quality crater happens
15:10:19 Liam: agreed, we have a script for immediate fanout to tertiary plus rate-limit to 20% until SRE confirms. We'll add that as part of the rollback checklist
15:10:33 Maya: switching gears, a couple of engineering notes: shadow scoring needs a stable dedupe key so we don't double-score same user sessions; also if you keep two models live remember to reconcile conversation state across variants
15:10:49 Priya: state reconciliation is our biggest worry — if the smaller model tokenizes differently we may get out-of-sync conversations
15:10:56 Liam: that's why we prefer same-tokenizer hedges; if you must change tokenizer we recommend a short state translation layer that maps conversation turns via normalized embeddings — it's extra work but preserves UX
15:11:12 Tom: will that add latency? embeddings-based translation sounds expensive
15:11:17 Liam: small overhead for translation, but it's a one-time cost per session and far cheaper than a full model call; plus you can cache the mapping for a session id
15:11:28 Sara: any notes on data residency if we fail to hosted during an outage? Our policy requires EU data stays in EU, does hosted fallback violate that?
15:11:37 Maya: hosted fallback to a different region would violate strict residency. For that scenario we recommend reserved dedicated pools in-region or a private deployment option. We'll flag region constraints in the matrix and mark any path that might move data cross-border
15:11:55 Priya: ok that helps. For the benchmark run, can you provide both raw logs and redwood-console-friendly artifacts? Our SRE needs raw traces for flamegraphing
15:12:05 Liam: yes raw traces and perf logs will be available. The micro-benchmark will emit JSON and a CSV summary you can ingest into your perf tools
15:12:16 Maya: any final risks we haven't covered?
15:12:20 Tom: only the SSO + firewall; otherwise i think we're good to proceed with the dry-run
15:12:25 Priya: one more small thing — what about concurrency throttling at the route level during failover? Can we set per-route throttles?
15:12:32 Liam: yes per-route throttles, and you can attach an escalation policy to increase concurrency gradually. We'll include an example throttle policy
15:12:44 Sara: last ask — please include a sample audit export showing rollback events, user who triggered, timestamps, and model version diffs
15:12:53 Maya: will do, i'll attach that to the security checklist and the dry-run invite
15:13:00 Maya: ok wrapping up. Recap of owners and timeline: Maya send pricing and hedging matrix by Monday, Liam share benchmark scripts this afternoon, Priya upload evals by 12/10, Sara firewall/KMS details by 12/07, Tom schedule dry-run for week of 12/08. Any objections?
15:13:18 Priya: none from me
15:13:21 Tom: good
15:13:23 Sara: good
15:13:30 Maya: great thanks all, we'll follow up in email with invites and docs. End call
15:13:36 Speaker 1: (call ended)
